Scientific Concept: Newton's Laws of Motion
Domain: physics / classical_mechanics
Definition: Three physical laws establishing the fundamental relationship between a body, the forces acting upon it, and its motion in response.

Principles:
1st Law (Inertia): A body remains at rest or in uniform linear motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
2nd Law (Force & Momentum): Net force equals time rate of change of linear momentum F = dp/dt = ma (for constant mass).
3rd Law (Action-Reaction): To every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force F_AB = -F_BA.

Experimental Proofs:
Cavendish torsion balance experiment (1798) verifying universal gravitation constant G
Atwood machine measurements validating F = ma in inertial reference frames

Applications:
Orbital trajectory calculation
Structural engineering
Ballistics
subject: Newton's Laws of Motion
